proposed_ledger_entry: Item 342 gives an exact all-row finite-field model for Item 339's integral selected carrier. With H=G^(p-r), Freshman's dream gives a_(r,n)=[u^n]H mod p and deg H=2p+2n. A plain multiplicative Fourier moment over F_p aliases exactly c_n, c_(n+p-1), and c_(n+2p-2), so its square-root bound does not isolate the forced coefficient. One moment over F_(p^2) isolates c_n exactly, but its square-root scale is p. Three Euler moments over F_p de-alias exactly through a 3x3 Vandermonde identity. Expanding those moments gives a Teichmueller lift T in Z[zeta_(p-1)] built from four fixed-support Kummer sums; every conjugate satisfies |sigma(T)|<=21 sqrt(p), and T reduces to a_(r,n) at one chosen prime above p. Since p splits completely and the coefficient field has degree phi(p-1), the norm bound (21 sqrt(p))^phi(p-1) is compatible with divisibility at one prime. Thus plain Fourier extraction plus black-box Weil bounds, with or without finite Euler de-aliasing, cannot by itself reduce the fixed-j1 ceiling. The transform reaches all rows, so the missing input is genuinely p-adic: chosen-prime nonconcentration, a unit-root theorem, bounded-degree descent plus exact trace nonvanishing, or a new relation controlling the two aliases. Booking and ceiling reduction remain zero; the fixed-j1 ceiling remains 1/36 per 6M.
